root_cause.text: A copy-paste mistake in `sound/usb/validate.c` registered the UAC3 AC header descriptor validator with `UAC_VERSION_2` instead of `UAC_VERSION_3`, so UAC3 headers skipped validation and could later be dereferenced unsafely.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `FIXED(UAC_VERSION_2, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor)` to `FIXED(UAC_VERSION_3, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor)`, and the CVE text states that this wrong version made the validator never match actual UAC3 devices, allowing truncated UAC3 headers to bypass validation and lead to out-of-bounds reads.

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct the validator to treat the UAC3 audio header descriptor as a UAC3-only structure.
intent_record.what: In the audio descriptor validator table, the `FIXED()` entry for `UAC_HEADER` was changed from requiring `UAC_VERSION_2` to requiring `UAC_VERSION_3`, while keeping the descriptor type and structure the same.
intent_record.how: At runtime, USB audio header descriptors matching the UAC3 header structure will now be validated only against UAC3 devices instead of incorrectly being accepted under the UAC2 version gate. This aligns the validator with the intended USB Audio Class version and prevents misclassification of UAC3 header descriptors.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the copy-paste mistake in the validator table for UAC3 headers: under the comment `/* UAC3 */` it registers `UAC_HEADER` with `FIXED(UAC_VERSION_2, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor),` instead of `UAC_VERSION_3`. This means a UAC3 AC header would not match the intended UAC3 protocol during `validate_desc()`, because matching requires `v->protocol == protocol` or `UAC_VERSION_ALL`. As a result, the UAC3 header validator is effectively skipped, which is the vulnerable construct described. There is no fix present in this snippet because the wrong protocol value is still `UAC_VERSION_2`, so `is_fixed` is false.
